title: Transpose of the open/closed compact-support coefficient square
statement: Let A and B be finite commutative rings, φ:A→B, and X,V,P,S Noetherian schemes. Let f:X→S and p:P→S be separated quasi-compact locally finite-type compactifiable maps, j:V→X a quasi-compact open immersion, and i:V→P a closed immersion, with j≫f=i≫p [open-closed-compact-scalar-coherence]. Write Q_T for derived scalar extension on the ordinary etale module derived category of T, ω_f,R=f_R^!(R_S), ω_p,R=p_R^!(R_S), and u_f,u_p for the specified counit-defined dualizing coefficient maps, R=A,B [def-per-exceptional-coefficient-maps]. Suppose ω_f,A is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Define b_i,M:Q_V(i_A^!M)→i_B^!(Q_PM) as the transpose of the inverse canonical direct-image scalarMate followed by Q_P of the proper closed counit. Proper finite coefficient extension makes that inverse defined [lem-asd-proper-finite-coefficient-extension]. There exist isomorphisms e_R:j_R^*ω_f,R≅i_R^!ω_p,R, R=A,B, with (openScalarRestriction φ j)_ω≫j_B^*(u_f)≫e_B=Q_V(e_A)≫b_i,ω_p,A≫i_B^!(u_p). No invertibility of b_i,M, u_f or u_p is assumed or concluded.

proof.text: The lower coefficient square supplies the two composite left-adjoint isomorphisms and their compatibility with the open and closed coefficient maps.
The existing open-mate and closed-assembly counit formulas, together with counit-mate-transport, construct the representing-object isomorphisms and prove the required transpose equality.

theorem closedOpen_dualizingMate_normalization
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (φ : A →+* B) {X V P S : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian V] [IsNoetherian P] [IsNoetherian S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [HasCompactification f]
    (j : V ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j]
    (i : V ⟶ P) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (p : P ⟶ S) [IsSeparated p] [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [QuasiCompact p]
    [HasCompactification p]
    (h : j ≫ f = i ≫ p)
    (hω : DerivedCategory.isBoundedConstructible A X
        (dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f) ∧
      ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn A X a b
        (dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f)) :
    ∃ (eA : (derivedRestriction (A := A) j).obj
          (dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f) ≅
        (rightDerivedUpperShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i).obj
          (dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) p))
      (eB : (derivedRestriction (A := B) j).obj
          (dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) f) ≅
        (rightDerivedUpperShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) i).obj
          (dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) p)),
      (openScalarRestriction φ j).hom.app (dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f) ≫
          (derivedRestriction (A := B) j).map
            (ExceptionalCoefficients.dualizingScalarMap φ f) ≫ eB.hom =
        (scalarExtension φ V).map eA.hom ≫
          closedDualizingCoefficientMate φ i (dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) p) ≫
          (rightDerivedUpperShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) i).map
            (ExceptionalCoefficients.dualizingScalarMap φ p)
